body.heading: The supply trap
paragraphs: It is tempting to believe the project will begin once you own the right notebook, the better camera, the proper tools. Sometimes that is true. More often it is a comfortable way to postpone starting.
Look around first. Scrap paper, a phone camera, leftover yarn, a borrowed instrument: most first versions can be made from what is already within reach.

body.heading: Scraps have their own charm
paragraphs: Working with limited materials forces inventive choices. A collage from old magazines, a meal from what is in the fridge, a garden in reused pots: constraints often produce the most personal results.
If the first version works, you will know exactly which upgrade would actually help, and you can save for that one thing instead of everything.

takeaway: Start with what is in the drawer; upgrade later, on evidence.
